title: "Broccoli Yield: Randomized Complete Block Analysis"

  bookdown::pdf_document2:
    keep_tex: true

    extra_dependencies: ["float"]
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE,
  fig.pos = "H",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5
)

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(emmeans)

# Download the workbook from GitHub.
# The source folder is 2-Data/Raw/.
github_base <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pr1nc3sso/",
  "Xilei-Living-cover-crop/master/2-Data/Raw/"
)

file_url <- paste0(
  github_base,
  "Broccoli%20harvest.xlsx"
)

file_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")

options(timeout = max(120, getOption("timeout", 60)))

status <- download.file(
  file_url,
  file_path,
  mode = "wb",
  method = "libcurl",
  quiet = TRUE
)

if (status != 0L) {
  stop("GitHub download failed. Check the URL.")
}

output_dir <- file.path(
  getwd(),
  "Yield_results"
)

dir.create(
  output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# Read the first nine columns.
raw <- read_excel(
  file_path,
  sheet = "living mulch",
  range = cell_cols("A:I"),
  col_types = "text"
)

names(raw) <- c(
  "harvest_date",
  "block",
  "treatment",
  "row_position",
  "fresh_weight_g",
  "grade",
  "appearance_note",
  "hollow_core",
  "marketable"
)

raw$excel_row <- seq_len(nrow(raw)) + 1L

dat <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(block, treatment, row_position, marketable),
      ~ na_if(toupper(trimws(.x)), "")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    if_any(
      c(block, treatment, row_position, fresh_weight_g),
      ~ !is.na(.x)
    )
  )

if (anyNA(dat[c("block", "treatment", "row_position")])) {
  stop("Missing identifiers. Check the source workbook.")
}

valid_rows <- c(
  "E", "EAST",
  "M", "MIDDLE", "CENTER", "CENTRE",
  "W", "WEST"
)

if (
  any(!dat$treatment %in% c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4")) ||
  any(!dat$row_position %in% valid_rows)
) {
  stop("Unexpected treatment or row labels.")
}

# Only middle-row heads enter the yield analysis.
dat <- dat %>%
  filter(
    treatment %in% c("T2", "T3", "T4"),
    row_position %in% c(
      "M", "MIDDLE", "CENTER", "CENTRE"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fresh_weight_g = as.numeric(fresh_weight_g)
  )

if (
  nrow(dat) == 0L ||
  anyNA(dat$fresh_weight_g) ||
  any(!is.finite(dat$fresh_weight_g)) ||
  any(dat$fresh_weight_g <= 0)
) {
  stop("Missing or invalid middle-row head weights.")
}

if (any(!dat$block %in% paste0("B", 1:4))) {
  stop("Unexpected block labels.")
}

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    block = factor(
      block,
      levels = paste0("B", 1:4)
    ),
    treatment = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("T4", "T3", "T2")
    )
  )

if (any(table(dat$block, dat$treatment) == 0L)) {
  stop("A plot has no harvest records; do not assume zero yield.")
}

# Enter the TOTAL area of one experimental plot, in square metres.
# This single value assumes all 12 experimental plots have equal areas.
# Do not use the biomass quadrat area.
plot_area_m2 <- 4 * 6.46

if (!is.finite(plot_area_m2) || plot_area_m2 <= 0) {
  stop(
    "Enter the confirmed total experimental plot area in plot_area_m2."
  )
}

# Pool all harvest dates within each experimental plot.
plot_data <- dat %>%
  group_by(block, treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    yield_kg = sum(fresh_weight_g) / 1000,
    heads = n(),
    mean_head_g = mean(fresh_weight_g),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    harvest_area_m2 = plot_area_m2 / 3,
    yield_t_ha = yield_kg / harvest_area_m2 * 10
  )

stopifnot(nrow(plot_data) == 12L)

# Fit the model using yield per unit area.
fit <- lm(
  yield_t_ha ~ treatment + block,
  data = plot_data
)

anova_result <- anova(fit)

# Adjusted treatment means and Tukey comparisons.
emm <- emmeans(
  fit,
  ~ treatment,
  weights = "equal"
)

emm_table <- as.data.frame(
  confint(
    emm,
    level = 0.95
  )
)

tukey_table <- as.data.frame(
  summary(
    pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"),
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
  )
)

# Confirmed mowing times relative to broccoli transplanting:
# T2: 1 week before, and 3 and 6 weeks after transplanting.
# T3: 1 week before, and 6 weeks after transplanting.
# T4: 1 week before transplanting only.
#
# Negative weeks indicate time before transplanting.
# Positive weeks indicate time after transplanting.
treatment_labels <- c(
  T4 = "T4\n-1 week",
  T3 = "T3\n-1 and +6 weeks",
  T2 = "T2\n-1, +3 and +6 weeks"
)
```

## Mowing schedule

All three treatments were mown one week before broccoli transplanting.
Additional mowing followed the treatment-specific schedule:

- **T2:** mown at 3 and 6 weeks after transplanting,
  giving three mowing events in total.
- **T3:** mown at 6 weeks after transplanting,
  giving two mowing events in total.
- **T4:** no additional mowing after transplanting,
  giving one mowing event in total.

The analysis compares these three treatment categories.
Mowing times and the number of mowing events are not entered
as continuous predictors.

## Response and experimental unit

The response is total harvested fresh yield in tonnes per hectare,
pooled over all recorded harvest dates. All weighed heads are included;
this is not marketable yield.

Each experimental plot has an area of `r plot_area_m2` square metres.
The effective harvested middle-row area is one-third of this area,
or `r plot_area_m2 / 3` square metres.

Yield in t/ha is calculated as harvested fresh weight in kg divided
by the effective harvested area in square metres, multiplied by 10.

The analysis includes three mowing treatments and four blocks.
Each block-by-treatment plot is one replicate. Outer rows and the separate
plastic-mulch sheet are not included.

With one response per plot, the treatment-by-block interaction cannot be
estimated separately from residual error. The model assumes additive
treatment and block effects.

```{r plot-data}
plot_display <- data.frame(
  Block = plot_data$block,
  Treatment = plot_data$treatment,
  Heads = plot_data$heads,
  Harvest_area_m2 = sprintf(
    "%.2f",
    plot_data$harvest_area_m2
  ),
  Yield_t_ha = sprintf(
    "%.2f",
    plot_data$yield_t_ha
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  plot_display,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Analysis of variance

Treatment and block are fitted as fixed factors. The design is balanced,
with treatment, block and residual degrees of freedom of 2, 3 and 6.

```{r anova}
# Format display tables without rounding the analysis objects.
format_p <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x),
    "",
    ifelse(
      x < 0.001,
      "<0.001",
      sprintf("%.3f", x)
    )
  )
}

a <- as.data.frame(anova_result)

anova_display <- data.frame(
  Source = rownames(a),
  df = as.integer(a$Df),
  SS = sprintf("%.2f", a[["Sum Sq"]]),
  MS = sprintf("%.2f", a[["Mean Sq"]]),
  F = ifelse(
    is.na(a[["F value"]]),
    "",
    sprintf("%.2f", a[["F value"]])
  ),
  p = format_p(a[["Pr(>F)"]])
)

knitr::kable(
  anova_display,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "ANOVA of harvested fresh yield (t/ha)"
)
```

## Adjusted treatment means

Means are adjusted for block and expressed in t/ha.
The table reports each estimated marginal mean, its model-based SE,
and its individual 95% confidence interval.
The figure shows means with error bars of one SE.

```{r adjusted-means}
emm_display <- data.frame(
  Treatment = emm_table$treatment,
  Mean = sprintf("%.2f", emm_table$emmean),
  SE = sprintf("%.2f", emm_table$SE),
  df = as.integer(emm_table$df),
  Lower = sprintf("%.2f", emm_table$lower.CL),
  Upper = sprintf("%.2f", emm_table$upper.CL)
)

knitr::kable(
  emm_display,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Adjusted yield means, SEs and 95% CIs (t/ha)"
)
```

## Tukey pairwise comparisons

All three pairwise treatment comparisons are of interest.
Tukey adjustment was therefore used to control the family-wise
Type I error rate across these comparisons. Comparisons are based
on estimated marginal means adjusted for block.

Differences, SEs and confidence limits are expressed in t/ha.
The confidence intervals and p-values below are Tukey-adjusted.

```{r tukey}
tukey_display <- data.frame(
  Contrast = tukey_table$contrast,
  Difference = sprintf("%.2f", tukey_table$estimate),
  SE = sprintf("%.2f", tukey_table$SE),
  df = as.integer(tukey_table$df),
  Lower = sprintf("%.2f", tukey_table$lower.CL),
  Upper = sprintf("%.2f", tukey_table$upper.CL),
  p = format_p(tukey_table$p.value)
)

knitr::kable(
  tukey_display,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Pairwise yield differences with Tukey-adjusted 95% CIs"
)
```

## Yield figure

Negative weeks on the horizontal axis indicate mowing before transplanting.
Positive weeks indicate mowing after transplanting.

```{r yield-figure}
#### add yield from the plastic mulch side, for reference

# Show plot yields and adjusted treatment means +/- 1 SE.
p <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = treatment,
    y = yield_t_ha
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    aes(shape = block),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_table,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(
      x = treatment,
      ymin = emmean - SE,
      ymax = emmean + SE
    ),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = emm_table,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(
      x = treatment,
      y = emmean
    ),
    shape = 18,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = treatment_labels
  ) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(
    x = "Mowing times relative to transplanting",
    y = "Harvested fresh yield (t/ha)",
    shape = "Block",
    caption = paste0(
      "Negative weeks: before transplanting; positive weeks: after transplanting.\n",
      "Small points = plots; diamonds = adjusted means; bars = +/- 1 model-based SE."
    )
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

print(p)
```

## Model diagnostics

Inspect residual spread and the normal Q-Q plot before interpreting the
tests. A non-significant Shapiro-Wilk test does not prove normality.

```{r diagnostics, fig.height=3.5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(fit, which = 1)
plot(fit, which = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

shapiro.test(residuals(fit))
```

```{r save-results, include=FALSE}
# Locate the local project root.
project_root <- normalizePath(
  getwd(),
  winslash = "/",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

repeat {
  required_folders <- file.path(
    project_root,
    c("2-Data", "5-Analysis")
  )

  if (all(dir.exists(required_folders))) break

  parent_dir <- dirname(project_root)

  if (identical(parent_dir, project_root)) {
    stop(
      "Run this Rmd inside the local Xilei-Living-cover-crop project."
    )
  }

  project_root <- parent_dir
}

# Export only the final yield figure to folder 7.
figure_dir <- file.path(project_root, "7-Extra")

dir.create(
  figure_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  plot_data,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Plot_yield.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  anova_result,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "ANOVA.csv"
  )
)

write.csv(
  emm_table,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Adjusted_means.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  tukey_table,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Tukey_comparisons.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  fit,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Yield_model.rds"
  )
)

ggsave(
  file.path(figure_dir, "Yield_ANOVA.png"),
  plot = p,
  width = 7,
  height = 4.5,
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)

ggsave(
  file.path(figure_dir, "Yield_ANOVA.pdf"),
  plot = p,
  width = 7,
  height = 4.5,
  bg = "white"
)

capture.output(
  sessionInfo(),
  file = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Session_info.txt"
  )
)
```
